## Problem 1

### Libraries

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(rvest)

set.seed(127)
```

## Birthdays

```{r}
birthdays = sample(1:365, size = 5, replace = TRUE)

repeated_birthdays = length(unique(birthdays)) < 5

birthday_results_df = 
  expand_grid(
    number_of_people = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    repeated = map_lgl(number_of_people, birthday_repeated)
  )

birthday_results_df |> 
  group_by(number_of_people) |> 
  summarize(prob_of_repeat = mean(repeated)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = number_of_people, y = prob_of_repeat)) +
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line()
```

## Problem 2

### Combining experimental and control data; tidying data

```{r}
long_study_df =
  tibble(
    file_path = c(list.files("data",full.names = TRUE))
  )

subjects_df =
  long_study_df |> 
  mutate(
    filename = basename(file_path),
    subject_id = str_remove(filename, "\\.csv$"),
    arm = if_else(str_starts(filename, "con"), "control", "experimental"),
    data = map(file_path, ~ read_csv(.x, show_col_types = FALSE))
  ) |> 
  unnest(data) |> 
   pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("week_"),
    names_to = "week",
    names_prefix = "week_",
    values_to = "observation"
  ) |> 
  mutate(week = as.numeric(week)) |> 
  select(subject_id, arm, week, observation)
```

### Spaghetti plot

```{r}
subjects_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = observation, color = arm)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = subject_id)) +
  geom_point()
```

* The control arm had overall less observations compared to the experimental arm The experimental arm observations increased over time while the control arm remained relatively level.
